title: Compatibility-signal taxonomy and onboarding contract for new open models
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Clarify the runtime compatibility metadata and acceptance contract for onboarding new open-model variants into the catalog. Deliver a small schema of compatibility signals, precise onboarding checklist (functional, perf, and provenance), and decision rules for pinning vs soft-pin vs unpinned experimental channels.
context: We onboard community/open model weights with varying runtime behaviors. Engineering has observed runtime regressions when a model was assumed to support streaming or prefix caching but did not. PM needs an operational metadata contract that model submitters fill and our runtime/console can consume to decide routing/pinning and automated fallbacks.
scope: Define the compatibility-signal taxonomy, required metadata fields for intake, the staged acceptance checklist, and automated suggestion rules for pinning. Produce a spec document and a small intake UI wireframe for Console team. Coordinate with Runtime, Ingest, and Security teams for required tests and provenance checks.
out_of_scope: Implementing the backend ingestion pipeline, UI code, or the actual runtime fallback heuristics. Full automation for pinning suggestions will be a follow-up (this ticket outputs the rules and example heuristics only).
requirements: Compatibility signal taxonomy with descriptions and enum values
Model intake schema additions (fields and expected formats) for the catalog UI and API
Onboarding checklist covering functional correctness, perf envelope, and provenance assertions
Decision rules for assigning: hard-pin, soft-pin, experimental-channel, or unpinned
Minimal runtime probe suite (3 smoke tests) that Runtime team will run in pre-ingest stage
Documentation and example JSON manifest for submitters
Acceptance criteria with measurable gates (latency, memory, KV correctness, streaming correctness)
compatibility_signals: runtime_features: list of supported capabilities (e.g., streaming, kv_cache, prefix_cache)
quant_profiles: declared quantization profiles tested (e.g., int8, q4_0)
seq_length_profile: expected 95th-percentile sequence length in tokens
batching_behavior: indicates if model benefits or regresses under batching
provenance: link or sha256 of model weights and training dataset declaration
signed_artifact: boolean indicating presence of signed model bundle
compat_score_hint: free-form numeric hint from submitter (0.0-1.0)
onboarding_checklist: Functional: model returns coherent responses for 10 provided developer test prompts
Streaming: if runtime_features includes streaming, must pass streaming correctness test (token order, no truncation)
KV cache: if kv_cache declared, must pass KV prefix reuse test (identical continuation with cached prefix)
Perf: 95th-percentile latency at target seq length within 2x of reference baseline for same family
Stability: no OOM on target hardware for N=3 runs of a 2k-token sequence
Security/Provenance: weights_sha256 must match submitted artifact and license clearly declared
Privacy: if training_data_declaration contains PII-sensitive sources, flag for Security review
pinning_rules: HARD_PIN: if provenance is absent OR runtime probe fails a functional test OR model exposes unsafe license
SOFT_PIN: if compatibility_signals indicate partial support (e.g., streaming supported but kv_cache missing) or perf on target GPU is 2-3x baseline
EXPERIMENTAL_CHANNEL: for models with signed_artifact=true, clear provenance, and pass smoke probes but lacking exhaustive perf validation
UNPINNED: small experimental forks with explicit disclaimer and in the discovery catalog only
acceptance_criteria: Spec doc reviewed and approved by Runtime and Ingest leads (comments resolved)
Onboarding checklist implemented as a human-readable checklist in Confluence linked from intake UI
Example manifest JSON and 2 sample model manifests added to repo (docs/catalog/example-manifests)
Wireframe for intake UI added to design ticket and linked in this ticket
Security has signed off on provenance and license validation requirements
Automated smoke-probe harness (3 tests) has a PR in github.com/redwood/runtime (PR #1286) and passes CI
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Submitters will mis-declare capabilities to get faster ingestion - Mitigation: runtime will verify declared signals with probes and mark mismatch for manual review
Risk: Strict pinning could block useful community models - Mitigation: experimental channel and temporary soft-pin paths with usage monitoring
Risk: Additional fields increase friction for intake - Mitigation: provide example manifests and an upload pre-fill tool in the UI
Risk: License/provenance mismatches could delay ingestion - Mitigation: allow a provisional review window (72 hours) and clearly surface missing artifacts
open_questions: What is the TTL for a soft-pin before re-evaluation (30 days suggested)?
Do we accept model bundles hosted on third-party sites or only signed artifacts stored in Redwood S3?
Should compat_score_hint be normalized by our ingestion service or left as advisory metadata?
What telemetry fields do Runtime and Console need to expose to signal degraded compatibility to customers?
decisions: Adopt a small, explicit compatibility signal set (see compatibility_signals) rather than a large free-form schema
Require a signed_artifact or explicit provenance link for models targeting catalog discovery
Use three onboarding outcomes: hard-pin, soft-pin (timeboxed), experimental-channel
Make security review mandatory if provenance URL is external or training data includes flagged sources
next_steps: Share draft spec with Runtime and Ingest for technical feedback by 2025-02-21
Add example manifests to docs repo and open PR#1286 for smoke-probe harness (assigned to eng)
Design to produce intake UI wireframe by 2025-02-25 (linked in comments)

Finalize spec and convert to Confluence onboarding checklist by 2025-03-05
